answer.why_different: The generated side omits the entire callback structure, including the runtime callback address, POST request body, and response definitions. This is a structural omission rather than a changed value.
answer.spec_3gpp: The 3GPP specification requires notifyMOIChanges to be mapped to an HTTP POST notification target, and defines NotifyMoiChanges as the notification payload. It also specifies a 204 success response with no body and ErrorResponse for failures.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI 3.0 defines callbacks as a map of possible out-of-band callbacks, with each callback value describing the initiated request and expected responses. A callback key must be a runtime expression identifying the callback URL.
answer.clearer_why: The official document explicitly shows the callback expression, POST operation, NotifyMoiChanges request body, and success and error responses. The generated side provides no callback definition, so it conveys no information about this notification mechanism.

```
expression = ( "$url" | "$method" | "$statusCode" | "$request." source | "$response." source )
source = ( header-reference | query-reference | path-reference | body-reference )
header-reference = "header." token
query-reference = "query." name
path-reference = "path." name
body-reference = "body" ["#" fragment]
fragment = a JSON Pointer [RFC 6901](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901)
name = *( char )
char = as per RFC [7159](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7159#section-7)
token = as per RFC [7230](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#section-3.2.6)
```  
The `name` identifier is case-sensitive, whereas `token` is not.
